changes.before: Handle omitted details without replacing empty text.
changes.after: Let a caller leave out a detail without losing empty text.

before: A question mark after a parameter name makes that argument optional. In note?: string, callers may omit note or explicitly pass undefined. Inside the body, reading note gives string | undefined, so handle the missing case before using string-only operations.
The required name comes first and the optional note comes last. This makes greeting("Ari") unambiguous. Optional does not mean that every kind of value is allowed; greeting("Ari", 3) is rejected.
Implement labelTask(title: string, detail?: string): string. Return title, a colon and space, then detail, using "No detail" only when detail is absent. Preserve an explicitly empty detail.
after: A question mark after a parameter name makes it optional. In `note?: string`, the caller may leave note out or pass undefined. Inside the function, note may be text or undefined.
The required name comes first and the optional note comes last. Optional does not mean any value is allowed. A numeric note is rejected, and this strict type does not allow null.
Make labelTask return title, a colon and space, then detail. Use No detail when detail is missing. Preserve an explicitly empty detail.
